title: Junji Ito’s Manga Horrors Hit Harder as Live-Action TV
gist: HBO Max is bringing the Japanese live-action horror anthology Strange: Junji Ito's Tales for Sleepless Nights to US audiences after a 12-episode TV Tokyo run this summer; director Yûta Shimotsu discussed the 'Face Thief' episode, season 2 plans including black-and-white, and a possible Uzumaki adaptation. A light culture piece with little market signal.

insights.claim: The 12-episode first season of live-action J-horror anthology Tales for Sleepless Nights aired on TV Tokyo this summer, and HBO Max is now releasing it to US audiences, with the first two episodes, 'Lovesickness (Part 1 of 3)' and 'The Bully', already available.
insights.speaker: Max Evry
insights.so_what: Streamers are licensing Japanese live-action horror for US catalogues; a minor data point on content sourcing for HBO Max.
insights.locator: Tales for Sleepless Nights aired its 12-episode first season

insights.claim: Ito's story 'The Bully' was previously animated for Netflix's Junji Ito Maniac, so the same IP is now being re-adapted across competing streamers in different formats.
insights.speaker: Max Evry
insights.so_what: Established manga IP is reused across formats and platforms, a low-cost content strategy to watch in streaming.
insights.locator: “The Bully” (previously animated for Netflix’s Junji Ito Maniac)

insights.claim: The Adult Swim 4-part anime adaptation of Ito's Uzumaki had a famously rocky production, with quality diving after the first episode so that the fourth installment had no director credit.
insights.speaker: Max Evry
insights.so_what: Production-quality risk in anime adaptations leaves room for a live-action Uzumaki, which Shimotsu named as his next preferred project.
insights.locator: When asked by a con attendee which of Ito's works

insights.claim: Director Yûta Shimotsu uses 'Face Thief' as a critique of conformity and peer pressure in Japanese society, saying there is social pressure not to be too different and individuality is not very respected.
insights.speaker: Max Evry
insights.so_what: Horror adaptations carrying social commentary can broaden appeal beyond genre fans.
insights.locator: We will not spoil the outcome

insights.claim: Shimotsu relies on stillness in performances and camerawork to evoke Ito's comic pages and hopes to push fidelity further in season 2 by shooting at least one episode in black-and-white, Ito's preferred mode of illustration.
insights.speaker: Max Evry
insights.so_what: Signals a possible season 2 and a stylistic bet; confirmation of a renewal would be the thing to watch.

insights.claim: Shimotsu says he is developing a Hollywood project, indicating the director may be moving into US production.
insights.speaker: Max Evry
insights.so_what: Minor talent-pipeline signal from Japanese horror to Hollywood; no detail provided.
insights.quote: I'm developing a Hollywood project, so see you soon.
insights.locator: “I would love to keep creating very bizarre
